diagnostic_evidence.quote: The constraints are expressed equivalently $\pvar_1 \leq 0$ and $\pvar_2 \leq - |\param|$.
The set-valued map \(\solp\) has nonempty values and is locally bounded.
However, as noted in Example~\myref{ex:failclarke}, this inclusion is strict in general

issues.failure_explanation: With F = x1 x2 and constraints x1 <= 0, x2 <= -|theta|, the minimizers include {(0,x2): x2 <= -|theta|} for every theta (and also {(x1,0): x1 <= 0} at theta = 0). The solution set is therefore unbounded for every theta, violating Assumption ass:specialcase(iii) and Assumption ass:standing(iii). The example verifies only MFCQ and f = 0. It thus lies outside the hypotheses of Theorem theo:mainsmooth and of the inclusion (eq:clarkesubdiffvf), which is stated under Assumptions ass:standing and relies on the level-boundedness required by the cited Theorem 10.13. It cannot show artifacts, or strictness of that inclusion, within the paper's framework, which is how the paper uses it.

failure_location.quote: We have $f(\param) = 0$ for all $\param \in \R$, and the MFCQ holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add compactifying smooth constraints, e.g. -1 - x1 <= 0 and -1 - theta^2 - x2 <= 0. These make the solution sets locally bounded while preserving MFCQ, f = 0, and the KKT point x* = (-1,0), lambda* = (0,0,1) with output u = 1. Then re-verify the assumptions in the example.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's sole illustration that ASM produces non-subgradient artifacts and that the Clarke-type inclusion is strict under the standing assumptions is not valid as stated. Remark rmk:consequenceasm(i), the introduction, and the related-work discussion rely on it.
issues.title: Artifact example violates the bounded-solution-set assumption it is meant to illustrate
issues.why_classification: A local modification of the example restores compliance with all assumptions and preserves its conclusion. No result or argument elsewhere changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \(\bar{g}\) is differentiable and locally Lipschitz on \(\Rell\)
is differentiable and path differentiable on \(\R^2\), continuously differentiable on \(\R^2 \setminus C\), and
even for locally Lipschitz, path differentiable and (point-wise) differentiable objective function with smooth constraints

issues.failure_explanation: Differentiability of g-bar at a point z of C, with gradient grad f-bar(z) = 0, requires the bump heights r_k phi(0) to be o(||z_k - z||), i.e. r_k = o(dist(z_k, C)). The proof only imposes r_k > 0, r_k -> 0 and disjointness, and then asserts differentiability without argument. These conditions do not suffice. Take C = {0} in R, z_k = 2^{-k}, r_k = 2^{-k}/4: all stated requirements hold, yet g-bar(z_k)/z_k >= phi(0)/4 > 0, while g-bar = f-bar on the left of 0, so the left derivative is 0. Hence g-bar is not differentiable at 0. The same issue arises for the fractal C.

failure_location.quote: consider \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k)\) such that \(r_k > 0\), \(r_k \xrightarrow[k \to \infny]{} 0\), and \(\Bcal(z_k,r_k) \cap \Bcal(z_{s},r_{s}) = \varnothing\) for \(s \neq k\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Additionally choose r_k <= dist(z_k, C)/k. For w in B(z_k, r_k) near z in C, the bump value is at most phi(0) r_k and ||w - z|| >= dist(z_k, C)(1 - 1/k), so the bump sum is o(||w - z||). Hence g-bar is differentiable on C with zero gradient there.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed pointwise differentiability of F in Claim theo:counterex(ii) is not established, so the advertised sharpness statement for differentiable, non-definable objectives is unsupported as written. Local Lipschitzness, C^1 regularity off C, the Clarke inclusion, and the failure of conservativity are unaffected.
issues.title: Bump radii not constrained relative to dist(z_k,C); differentiability on C unsupported
issues.why_classification: One extra condition on the radii and a short estimate restore the full statement. The construction and every conclusion of both claims are preserved.
